column1: # Executive summary: audited sections 11.1 through 11.5, spec lines 1666-1848, against main HEAD 3cc63c55ed04df7035c1c06a8cc754e20a0b1ce1. Scope covered
# 104 PR rows and 126 extracted cite records, including three implicit same-file cites that row prose expressed as bare line numbers. Verification used
# git show main:<path> blobs only. Git Bash sed is broken in this environment with Win32 error 5, so line selection was reproduced from git-show output
# with PowerShell/Python indexing after confirming sed failure. Result: 23 valid, 39 stale, 3 out-of-file, and 61 not-found/no-line records. Pattern is
# severe cite rot, not isolated typo drift. Most stale rows resolve to real files but wrong code: shifted handlers, renamed Unity plugin paths, old
# audit line numbers, and prose cites that point at adjacent comments or unrelated functions. Several PR rows have no numeric file:line cite at all,
# especially new-file, dependency, Unity, and doc-cleanup work; those cannot be independently verified by the requested line-probe method. High-risk
# stale clusters: pipeline topo/default-pass/depth lines, W-1 water migration lines, Unity importer parity rows, asset-budget lod_meshes cites, and
# Batch15 doc backfill cites. Valid notable anchors remain for chunk size, shadow scanline bytes, macro-color consumed channels/palette, waterfall foam
# inversion, determinism artifact test, Quixel linear blend, v6 splat truncation, and selected old-wrong-cite confirmations. Treat this runway as
# needing citation repair before dispatch; otherwise agents will patch wrong sites. Recommended next move: repair stale cites before assigning PR
# owners, then rerun this audit after each spec edit so dispatch packets carry verified anchors only now.
